witness_description: Take [a,b]=[0,1], E=W=X=R with the usual norm and identity injections, p=1, q=2, and R=1. Let g(x)=2 dist(x,Z) and u_n(t)=g(2^n t) for n>=0. The identity E->W is compact because R is finite-dimensional. Each u_n has L1 norm 1/2 and is Hölder-1/2 with its own constant 2^(n+1), so every u_n belongs to S. For every distinct m,n, the exact L1 distance between u_m and u_n is 1/3.
refutation_explanation: The sequence (u_n) is an infinite 1/3-separated subset of S in L1([0,1];W), hence has no Cauchy or convergent subsequence. Therefore S is not precompact. The growing constants 2^(n+1) demonstrate precisely why individual, nonuniform Hölder constants do not yield the asserted conclusion.
search_space: Exhaustive lexicographic sweep of 16 templates: p=1; q in {2,3}; R in {1,1/2}; amplitude A in {1,1/2}; and frequency base B in {2,3}. For every template the program checks the exact L1 bound, the individual Hölder implication, and the closed-form even-B separation certificate; it also exactly integrates frequency gaps 1 through 6 as a certificate check. The selected template is (p,q,R,A,B)=(1,2,1,1,2). The finite template sweep finds an analytically certified infinite family; the six-gap check is not treated as exhaustive evidence about precompactness.
